Q3.question: Clean the Wasp stock export (remove title rows, blank rows, repeated header, test/total rows; normalise part numbers; remove duplicates keeping the first). How many distinct valid parts are left?
Q3.definition: Rows after: Skip 2 + promote; remove blank rows; remove repeated header; keep only rows whose Item Number normalises to PRT-0000 (uppercase, remove spaces/hyphens/nbsp, strip 'PRT', pad digits to 4, prefix 'PRT-'); Remove Duplicates on normalised Item Number keeping the FIRST row.
Q3.how: Normalise Item Number with a custom function, filter nulls, Table.Buffer then Remove Duplicates on Item Number; count rows.

Q4.question: After adding the Stock Status conditional column (Total Available = 0 -> Out of stock; <= 5 -> Reorder; else OK), how many parts are 'Out of stock'?
Q4.definition: Stock Status on the de-duplicated 60 parts using the keep-first Total Available. Counts: Out of stock 8, Reorder 8, OK 44.
Q4.how: Add Column > Conditional Column on Total Available, then Group By / filter on Stock Status.

Q5.question: What is the total stock value at Wasp Item Cost: the sum of Total Available × Item Cost over the 60 de-duplicated parts (keep the first row of each duplicate)? Where Item Cost is N/A or an error (#REF!), treat the cost as blank, so that part adds £0. Round to 2 dp.
Q5.definition: Item Cost: remove '£' and ',' and convert; 'N/A' and #REF! errors become null and contribute 0 (4 parts). Sum of Total Available x Item Cost over the 60 de-duplicated parts, rounded 2dp.
Q5.how: Replace Errors on Item Cost, try Number.From otherwise null, add Total Available * Item Cost (null -> 0), sum.

Q10.question: After cleaning the Xero payable invoice detail (fix dates, prices and item codes; remove - do not net off - the 3 credit-note lines and remove the near-duplicate lines, keeping the first), what is the total invoice value ex VAT, i.e. the sum of Quantity × Unit Price (ex), to 2 dp?
Q10.definition: Cleaned Xero lines = 150 (credit notes removed, duplicates removed on Reference + normalised Item Code, keep first). Value = sum(Quantity x Unit Price (ex)).
Q10.how: Skip 4 rows, filter Source <> Payable Credit Note, normalise codes/dates/prices, Remove Duplicates, add Quantity*Unit Price, sum.

Q11.question: Using KR's valuation rule, what is the total stock valuation across the 60 parts, to 2 dp? Price = the latest Xero invoice Unit Price (by Invoice Date, credit notes excluded); else the latest Purchase Log Net Unit Price (by Date, cancelled lines excluded); else the Wasp Item Cost. Stock Value = Total Available × Price.
Q11.definition: Price = latest Xero Unit Price (Invoice Date, credit notes excluded) else latest Purchase Log Net Unit Price (Date, CANCELLED excluded) else Wasp Item Cost. Ties on date broken by higher Reference/PO number. Stock Value = Total Available x Price (2dp each), summed over 60 parts.
Q11.how: Wasp_Clean + latest-per-part from Xero_Clean and PurchaseLog_Clean via Table.Sort/Table.Distinct, left joins, waterfall conditional columns, sum Stock Value.

Q12.question: (a) What unit price (2 dp) does the valuation use for PRT-0015? (b) Which source does it come from, and why is it not the price on the most recent Xero line for that part?
Q12.definition: PRT-0015 has a later credit note in Xero (unit price 148.53, dated after its latest invoice). The credit note is excluded, so the latest invoice line dated 06/02/2026 sets the price. Answer format: price | source.
Q12.how: Filter out the credit note, take the latest dated invoice line for the part; it exists in Xero so the source is Xero.

Q13.question: After removing duplicate receipts (same Ref, keep the first) and treating the (150.00) refund as a negative amount, what is the total of ALL Q1 receipts, including the two receipts from non-customers, to 2 dp?
Q13.definition: 123 receipts after Remove Duplicates on Ref (keep first). Amounts: '£' text and '(150.00)' brackets parsed (refund = -150.00). Sum of Amount.
Q13.how: ParseAmount, dedupe on Ref, sum Amount.

Q14.question: How much did Flintwood Marine Ltd pay in Q1 (net of its refund), and how many payments is that? Count only positive receipts as payments; the refund reduces the total but is not a payment.
Q14.definition: Receipts matched to Flintwood Marine Ltd via ExtractPayer + Fuzzy_Transform_Table, after de-duplication. £ paid = net sum including the (150.00) refund; # payments = count of positive receipts (refund not counted).
Q14.how: Extract payer, fuzzy join with transformation table, group by customer: sum Amount and count positive amounts.

Q15.question: After matching with the supplied Fuzzy_Transform_Table, which receipts (Ref numbers) remain unmatched to any customer?
Q15.definition: Refs whose extracted payer text is not a customer and not in Fuzzy_Transform_Table: 10131 (CASH DEPOSIT) and 10132 (J SMITH BUILDERS); combined value 3375.50. Fuzzy matching at 0.8 alone without the table is approximate - confirm on the day.
Q15.how: After the fuzzy join, filter Customer Matched = null (UNMATCHED).
